The 1st Battalion was being brought up to strength in town and it had between 500 and 600 men, and there was a military police company there; and those were the men who were present in town. But you must be aware of the fact that the 1st Battalion and one of its company was in Vrse; the other was at the entrance to Gornji Vakuf, in the part of town we call the Gornja Mahala; and the third company was in the lower part of town so to speak, whereas the 3rd Battalion was in the lower part of the municipality, to the left of Radusa and to the right towards Vojska.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation if the general has anything other to ask you about, he may do so. I would now like to have a look at the documents on the basis of which General Petkovic's order dated the 15th of January was issued very briefly.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D 00341. It's a regular combat report from the command of the North-western Croatia operative zone dated the 13th of January, 1993. I'll just mention two matters here -- North-western Herzegovina my colleagues have told me that I made a mistake. It's a report from the command of the operative zone of North-western Herzegovina, and I quote. It says: "In the village of Luzine Croatian houses were torched and Croats were expelled towards the positions held by our units." Tell me, do you have any information according to which houses were torched and Croats were expelled from that village?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of January, that evening I went with Mr. Zrinko Tokic to the village that you had to pass through to Pajic Polje; I think that's where the battalion command was located. I couldn't leave the vehicle because they couldn't guarantee my safety. Zrinko told me that they couldn't guarantee my safety because an HVO member had died; that's what he said when he got into the vehicle. I can't remember his name, the name of his soldier. I knew his brother though. Apparently he had been massacred. I even asked him how he had been massacred, and then he said that he had been circumcised in the Muslim way, cut up in the Muslim way, but I know that there are two Croatian houses in the village of Luzine itself. Nothing happened to anyone else. Luzine has a Bosniak majority, there are only two Croatian families.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You're saying that nothing happened to anyone else. You're saying the inhabitants of those two houses suffered a certain fate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about this soldier, but those soldiers attacked Luzine from Pajic Polje, and that's why we went to Pajic Polje, to Grnica, and to Hrasnica, and to Duratbegovic Dolac, and to Drazev Dolac that evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll clarify that later. Let's have a look at the next document, 4D 00356. It's an extraordinary report, an interim report, from Zeljko Siljeg dated the 13th of January. I'll just emphasise two items. "The passage from Vakuf and the entry to Vakuf has been blocked, and in the course of the night fighter -- fire was opened from infantry weapons and mortars from the direction of Zelene."

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 356. Tell me, do you have any information according to which there was such a blockade?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the HVO had implemented that blockade; the town was under attack. On the 13th of January, the town was attacked and as a result it was under a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you have no information about ABiH activity?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the armija was defending itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You were defending yourselves; the HVO said they were defending themselves. We'll see what the documents say. We're now discussing the 13th of January. Are you aware of the fact that after all these events the Main Staff of the HVO tried to find a peaceful solution to the problems in Gornji Vakuf. You mentioned the arrival of Colonel Andric. Are you aware of any other attempts that were made?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday in answer to a Prosecution question I said that yes attacks were carried out, but today I said that it wasn't possible to talk to Colonel Siljeg about that subject; he only made threats.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about the other HVO officers that you had contact with? Were you able to reach any agreements with them to discuss matters to try and find a peaceful solution to the problems?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first spoke to Tokic, Zrinko, since I knew him well; he told me that no one asked him about anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, you also cooperated well with Colonel Andric. I'd like to show you an order issued by my client, General Petkovic. P 01115 is the number in my bundle. It's an order dated the 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: P 01115. It's an order on avoiding incidents and a request is made to find a peaceful solution to problems to establish contact with the Muslim side. Were you familiar with this Main Staff attempt to find a peaceful solution to the problems in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't familiar with this document dated the 13th of January. But given what was being done by UNPROFOR -- well, yes, attempts were made, I can't say that wasn't the case, but you'll have to ask Colonel Siljeg about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'll show you just an another two documents that preceded this order dated the 15th of January. The first one is number 4D 00349. Please have a look at the document. It's a report from the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade dated the 14th of January, and I'd like to draw your attention to two parts of the document. Have a look at the middle of the page. It says: "In the ABiH there are many soldiers from Jajce who have lingered in Gornji Vakuf together with their equipment and materiel, and when withdrawing, when Chetniks were taking Jajce, there were soldiers from Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, and Kupres. There are many men under arms on the Muslim side." And then in the last -- in the penultimate paragraph it says: "From 1500 to 1700 hours scores of business premises belonging to Croats were set on fire in the lower part of the village of Bistrica." There are other important passages but we don't have time to go into all the details in the document. Can you comment on the strength of ABiH members in the area of Gornji Vakuf? I'm not just referring to the town of Gornji Vakuf but to the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there was a battalion in Voljevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about Donji Vakuf, Bugojno, Kupres?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about the units from that area?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. During that period of time there wasn't a single unit from Bugojno and Donji Vakuf in Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to refugees and able-bodied men from the area?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that was a negligible number because when the army was established in Bugojno the Defence secretariats returned all individuals from Donji Vakuf and they formed a Donji Vakuf unit in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about torching of business premises belonging to Croats in the village of Bistrica, do you have any information about this?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you know Bistrica. There aren't even ten houses in the lower part of Bistrica. I don't know which facilities you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need a clarifications. The soldiers from Jajce who came to Gornji Vakuf, how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number changed from day-to-day. There were -- there weren't under 400. At the time the battalion had 400 men, perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 400. Did they have a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had a commander. Mr. Halid Dedic was the commander but they weren't armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the 400 soldiers under the command of the -- of Halil Deric weren't armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can claim with full responsibilities that many they weren't armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In such a situation, who provided or who represented military authority? Was it yourself or Deric who had come from Jajce, who was from Jajce? This battalion from Jajce, were -- was it subordinated to you or was it in fact simply in your town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in Voljevac and Halil reported directly to the 3rd Corps commander. It was never subordinated to the 317th or to the TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How far is Voljevac from Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Twelve kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Twelve kilometres. Is it possible - and this is what the Defence seems to be suggesting on the basis of this document - is it possible that parts of this battalion committed acts of -- or excessive acts in Bistrica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they weren't in Bistrica. They couldn't have reached Bistrica because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what is stated in the document is false?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's false.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: One more document. 4D 00350. The document is also from Dr. Ante Starcevic's brigade dated the 15th of January, and it, among other things, refers to an artillery attack from the direction of Muslim villages on villages inhabited by Croats. Can you tell us anything about that day, that is the 15th of January, whether the information contained in this report are correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are incorrect, because units in this area didn't have a single artillery weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We, the Judges, who are used to documents, we see that there is a series of documents that -- who -- the contents of which is being disputed, and therefore we are told about events that did not take place. As far as you are concerned, what would be the reason for this type of reference? What would be the aim? Those who compiled these reports, why would they contain erroneous information? Do you have an explanation for that? Was it because the collected information was not reliable? Was it because it, as you appear to have said, they wanted to make progress and went beyond what was actually happening, or were there any other reasons that we're not aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at these documents for the first time, and as far as I'm able to judge, they are incorrect. But I do know that from Drazevo, Duratbegovic Dolac, and Drazeni, on the 15th here no artillery fire could have been opened because the units there didn't have artillery weapons. The signature here is my former teacher Ivan Kraljevic. I'm sorry that we don't have a document in which he says that 12 civilians were killed in Dusa, and it doesn't say what was undertaken. However, the behaviour of Colonel Siljeg during the negotiations, because there were negotiations in this period of time as well at UNPROFOR headquarters, show that the documents were a justification for the situation imposed by the HVO in Gornji Vakuf. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance. The brigadier, when referring to artillery, has in mind more than a hundred millimetres. Maybe the report refers to 82-millimetre mortars. Could 82-millimetre mortars have been positioned there which he considers artillery and you do not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, the company in Drazev Dolac and Duratbegovic Dolac and the company from Zrnci [phoen] that covered Luzani didn't have 82-millimetres at the time. The mortars of this battalion were near Raduski Kamen, as you know, in the period referred to by this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank General Praljak. I was going to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Brigadier Agic, tell us, since these HVO documents contained certain erroneous information, do you believe that the HVO of Gornji Vakuf provided false information about the situation on the ground to the Main Staff of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that; you'll have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you have reviewed these documents and judged them in this way, I would like -- my question is to summarise all your answers. If you wish to make a comment. If you don't wish to answer that question, we can move on. I should like to show you another document relating to the numerical strength of the BH army in the area of Gornji Vakuf. So look at document 4D 00375. From the operative zone of North-western Herzegovina on the 17th of January containing the following fact: 2.900 soldiers, 317th Mountain Brigade; then the army staff of 300 men; the military police, 150 men; and the reserve police force, 150 men. These units of the 305th Mountain Brigade from Jajce have been added. You -- there is a mention of the figure of 500, I think you said 400. Then there are the Green Dragons, 100 men. And then another unit arrived last night numbering 30 persons from Bugojno and nine others from Novi Travnik. Tell us, are these figures about the numerical strength of the BH army on the 17th of January correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to have a closer look. There's a mirror here. The brigade had three battalions. The commander of the 1st Battalion was Sero Edin [phoen], correct; 2nd Battalion, Milanovic; and the 3rd Battalion -- but there was no 4th battalion. Mr. Fuad Zec was in the 3rd Battalion, deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we please limit our comments to the numbers.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units from Jajce was not in Crnica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: You cannot expect us Judges to follow --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I will repeat. So please try to understand. You cannot expect us Judges to follow everything those numbers when you are speaking in your mother tongue and you are very fast, and simply when we see first time these documents in English - even there are some documents which have not been translated - you cannot expect us to make a real judgement if those numbers are correct or not or they are in good -- they are really showing something very important to us. So I would ask the -- actually Ms. Alaburic to -- merely to single out some of the most important elements which she thinks that it is very important for us, also for the Bench to know. And after this we will make our own judgement. But if you are having a dialogue between you, Ms. Alaburic, and also Brigadier Agic, it will not help too much if you are just answering to each other and competing with each other. So it is my advice to cool down a bit, to slow down a bit, and then only to talk about the most important elements. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, in view of what my colleague has just said, what is important for us quite clearly is to examine this document and to check against what you are saying. In this document there are figures. The description given by HVO of your unit, does it correspond to the situation such as you knew it to be? If not, tell us where the mistakes are or the estimates.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no 4th Battalion. There was no Green Dragon unit in the area of Gornji Vakuf in this period of time. The first unit that came to Gornji Vakuf from outside its territory was on the 19th of January, just before Bistrica fell. A platoon came from Bugojno consisting of 24 men. The commander of that platoon was Faruk Aganovic known as Jupi, and there were no other units in this area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, one more question in connection with this document dated the 17th of January. It will help in understanding the relations. In the lower part of the page there's a sentence which reads, you will find it, I hope: "In Voljica from the positions in Radusa and Skrte, soldiers withdrew and regrouped." Is this a situation when the BH army withdrew from positions towards the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It just reduced the strength of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander withdrew a part of the men for the conflict with the HVO. Is that right.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I be told how much time I have left so I can decide how to proceed with my cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've used 49 minutes. Normally you are entitled to one hour, unless there are other counsels who will give you some of their time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that two Defence counsels will not have any more questions, we have shared amongst ourselves their time, so I will have another half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, tell me, please, after the 18th of January and the events in Gornji Vakuf, I have a large number of documents, but perhaps we need not go into each of them, how did the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina act?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 19th and the signing of the cease-fire, the army was mostly defending itself because we were inferior in every respect except, perhaps, in certain areas in numerical strength; but in terms of equipment we could not compare.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So as far as manpower is concerned, you were not inferior?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "in certain places."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any artillery or mortar actions by the BH army against certain HVO positions?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 20th of January, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at document 4D 00391; it is a document of the command of the 3rd Corps dated the 18th of January, 1993. It is a report on the units of the HVO which says, among other things: "Information with relations of the HVO. "During the morning and in the evening an order was issued to the artillery of Novi Travnik to open fire on targets defined by the command of the 317th Mountain Brigade and the municipal defence staff of Gornji Vakuf." Can you tell me whether this sentence is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the army, until the 19th, did not fire with artillery. This is correct, because a request was addressed and aid was sought.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next sentence: "From Bugojno a Sabotage Detachment was sent towards Gornji Vakuf to cover Pajic Polje, Trnovaca and two sabotage groups were infiltrated into Raznik and Drazen Polje to assist the Bugojno detachment," which means that that detachment was already there. Tell me, is this true from this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With exception of these two infiltrated groups, the rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Then it says that: "The command of the 317th Mountain Brigade and the municipal TO Staff of Bugojno propose that a unit be addressed to Makljen to arrive in the morning. It could change the situation in Gornji Vakuf." Tell me, did you ask for aid to capture Makljen?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is out of the question. We would need much more to capture Makljen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Will you now look at document 4D 00360; it is an order by commander Arif Pasalic dated the 19th of January, 1993. Ordering to the Neretvica Brigade, together with units of the Prozor battalion, capture Makljen. Did you have any knowledge of this order?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see this for the first time, but I know with full responsibility that no such attempt was ever made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Look at document 4D 00361; it is a document of the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, to the command of the 4th Corps saying: "I have asked for an answer whether Neretvica has been sent on assignment and has it arrived." Did you expect aid for Makljen?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an unrealistic assignment at the time, and I didn't know that such an order was existed but -- such an assignment existed. Well, I see from this document that it did, but it was unrealistic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Will you now look at document under Prosecution number, but in my set of documents, P 01210, an extraordinary combat report by Cikotic on the 19th of January.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 01210. So let us jointly examine certain parts of that document. In point 1 it says: "In activities so far we have lost the villages Uzricje, Dusa, lower part of Hrasnica." Can you tell me what does it means "we have lost those villages." Does it mean that the army held them until then?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true for Uzricje and the lower part of Hrasnica, but not for Dusa.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 it says: "The plan is that we execute sabotage actions during the night in several directions." So I repeat paragraph 2 says that: "The plan is that we execute sabotage actions during the night in several directions," and certain directions are mentioned. Is that true? Tell us please.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you read paragraph 3 for us, please, these five requests.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read them aloud?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, and will you comment on them straight away to see whether they're right or not, or is Cikotic speaking falsely.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To ensure a man who will reach the village of Bistrica, take-over command of the anti-armour company from Novi Travnik, Mujahedin forces from Bistrica, and together with them carry out an attack along the direction check-point Bistrica-Franjkovac-Krupa-Ziza-Gornji Vakuf. Link up with forces in town and provide us with the TMS that is already there. "2. From the direction of Konjic provide all kinds of aid and supply from Voljevac."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please, for the record.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "3. Lendo should accept our requests and open artillery fire upon indicated targets, but from Bugojno Sabotage Detachment under command of Jupi should be designed to reach Gornji Vakuf - he knows along which route. Also convey to the people of Bugojno that reinforcements in manpower should be sent by them together with command staff and that they should not return before executing their task. "5. Send the infantry weapons to the fighters of the 305th Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have to admit that I'm not quite sure whether everything has been recorded in the transcript. I see that item 4 hasn't been recorded. Perhaps there was someone who was follow the transcript. I'll repeat what item 4 says, since it hasn't been recorded in the transcript. Item 4 states the following: "From Bugojno it is necessary to urgently send anti-Sabotage Detachment, commanded by Faruk Aganovic, Jupi. Its task will be to break through to Gornji Vakuf. He knows along which axis this should be done. Similarly, convey to the people of Bugojno that they are sending reinforcements together with the necessary command staff and they should not return before the task has been carried out." My question is: Were these requests met, and is that how the ABiH acted in military terms?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1 wasn't implemented. Item 2 was the main line of -- for supplies in -- during that period. Item 4 was partially carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. At the time of this combat activity, were ABiH representatives involved in negotiations with the HVO in order to find a peaceful solution to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's time for break now, or perhaps I can continue with the cross-examination. I've lost track of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to clarify something because the Judges will have decide whether it was the HVO or the ABiH initiated the conflict. This is dated the 12th of January -- the 19th of January --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 1993, 1530 hours. It's a special report, a special combat record. In the first paragraph it says: "In the afternoon hours the HVO forces launched an attack in the direction of the village of Vrse which was shelled," et cetera. There was other action and Uzricje and Dusa and parts of Hrasnica were lost. Given the contents of the document, we seem to have a description of the events that were unfolding -- or it was the HVO that had taken these villages subsequent to shelling, et cetera. In the second paragraph there seems to be a suggestion made by Cikotic to counter this action, to take action in the night between the 19th and the 20th, and engage in sabotage action in number of directions. And the third item concerns requests, various requests, submitted to the 3rd Corps. So how do you analyse this document? Is this a document that was sent to the 3rd Corps in order to describe the situation, to inform them of the fact that you're going to react and also to ask for support, various kinds of support. What is your point of view as far as this document is concerned? This document comes from the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in this part of the report, sir -- well, they wanted to say that the situation was dramatic. At the time the town was about to fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that is the first paragraph; that's the part of the document that you're referring to. And what about the second paragraph? Is this an action plan for the 317th in order to face up to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't remember this being the 317th's plan or a plan conceived by its commander because this item seems quite unrealistic. It would have been difficult to comply with what's stated in this item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So why has this been noted if you believe that it's not realistic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I suppose it was to justify the requests being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. I see that it mentions the Mujahedin. Could the Mujahedin have been of any use as reinforcements for ABiH units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about these Mujahedin, because at the time in Central Bosnia there wasn't a single Mujahedin unit. I don't know which Mujahedin being referred to. The El Mujahid unit was formed after this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of that is -- point of clarification. Is the gentleman saying under oath that there were no Mujahedin at this period of time? That's what I want to know. I'm not talking about a unit. I'm talking about Mujahedin, because they were coming and going, they were working in groups, and, as we all know, on both sides they were feared. So I want -- I want a clear answer on this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am declaring under oath that during this period of time, and even later, not a single Mujahedin participated in combat in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, General. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask you to put a question to this witness or allow me to do so. Mr. Agic, as the commander of the defence staff in Gornji Vakuf -- well, that was the command of the 317th Brigade there. It was stronger than his -- than him, and in Gornji Vakuf his superior command was through Selmo Cikotic. I'd like to know who the top commander in Gornji Vakuf was. Was it you, or was it the commander of the 317th Brigade, or was it Selmo Cikotic? Could you answer that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jusuf Heljic was the brigade commander. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I'm not asking who he was, but who was the most responsible or highest-ranking commander in the area of Gornji Vakuf. Was it you at the time, were you in command of the 317th Brigade and the Janjac Brigade and all the other sabotage forces? Or was it the commander of the 317th Brigade who was in charge? Or was it Selmo Cikotic, who was your superior because he was from the 3rd Corps and he was sent there by the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By order of the corps commander when these -- this fighting broke out, I was only responsible for the town. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] We're talking about the municipality of Gornji Vakuf. Who was spot responsibility for the entire area of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For -- well, he was responsible for the brigade. Heljic, Jusuf, was responsible for the brigade. He was in command of the brigade; that didn't change. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I know who was in command of the brigade. Who was in command of the territory of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf? Who was in charge of your brigade and yourself and all the units who arrived there? There were three of you there. Let me assist you. You were there. You weren't in command, you said. There was the 317th Brigade command and there was Selmo Cikotic from the 3rd Corps. Who is the highest-ranking officer? Only one such person can exist. Can you provide us with a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer your question in that way. By order issued by the corps command, I was appointed for the defence of the town. You'll probably be able to find that order somewhere. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Who did the 317th Brigade have to report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the 3rd Corps. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Who was in Gornji Vakuf from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Selmo Cikotic. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Did that mean that Selmo Cikotic was responsible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He had to report to Enver Hadzihasanovic as the commander of the of the 3rd Corps. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Did the 317th Brigade and its commander have to report to Selmo Cikotic? And therefore -- through him, did they have to report to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] It can't be partial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever Cikotic suggested as a member of the corps command had to go to Zenica, and then this had to be returned to him with a signature. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Let me ask you the following question: Who was senior in terms of their position, you or Selmo Cikotic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was Selmo Cikotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt again, but please be so kind to slow down; the interpreters are begging you. And don't interrupt each other when you speak, but please wait until the interpreters will actually interpret one of the statements and then you continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Petkovic is putting a very important question to you, and this is what we all have to know. On the 19th of January, who was the highest-ranking military officer in the 317th Brigade, was it Mr. Cikotic or yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cikotic wasn't from the 317th; he was in the territory of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf on behalf of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In military terms, who was the most responsible individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was for the town. For the units outside the town it was the brigade commander, Jusuf Heljic. Selmo Cikotic was there on behalf of the corps command, and it was his responsibility to coordinate certain activities. He was didn't have the authority to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That is your military analysis, and it's in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina that were in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I have one brief question. Selmo Cikotic is more senior than you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Sir, why -- how is it that you have a right to comment on a report of someone who is senior to you? I don't understand. How do you have a right to comment on a report drafted by Selmo Cikotic in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as a member of the corps he didn't have the authority to issue orders. One knew who had the right to issue orders in the corps. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Well, I know who issued orders in the corps. Selmo Cikotic forwarded certain information to the 3rd Corps, and he obtained this information from you, the commander of the 317th Brigade, from the commander of the Jajce Brigade, and from all the other forces; and he unified all this and sent it to the commander of the 3rd Corps. And now you are saying that your superior wasn't telling the truth. I can understand that in the case of the Ante Starcevic Brigade, but in the case your own superior, to say that he wasn't telling the truth --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I did not say that he did not gather information. I'm not saying that he didn't obtain information. I said that he was not in command, and I also added -- and I'll repeat this now. I'm not sure what he meant when he said the "Mujahedin." You tell me which area he they could have come from. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, from Ravno Rostovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There was a platoon of the 7th Muslim in Ravno Rostovo, and we know who the commander was. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] We'll deal with that later, but Selmo Cikotic was superior to all of you, whether you agree with that or not and you -- you know that. That's all I'd like to say, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you have a look at the document in B/C/S signed by Cikotic. Have a look at the top, and to the left I can see that it says the 317th Gornji Vakuf Brigade and there's a number 01/3693. In the 317th Brigade you filed reports or orders. How was it possible to record this document in the list of documents of the 317th Brigade? Can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The brigade had packet communications, where all documents received and sent were registered. Mr. Selmo Cikotic was entitled to use such packet communications because he regularly reported about negotiations, and with his signature he was entitled to use the packet and send a report in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in brief, when he sent this report to the 3rd Corps you were not informed at all of the contents of this document. He didn't speak to you about it? He didn't ask you for your opinions on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many of the reports that he sent I was aware of. I also was aware of certain discussions with UNPROFOR. I wasn't in the brigade command then; I was somewhere else then -- I didn't know if I was somewhere else. And I wasn't present when he may have sent certain reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but apparently you discovered this report quite recently. You were not aware of its existence on the 19th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This particular one I did not see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because if you had seen it, you would have told him that the sabotage activities in the zone as described here were unachievable? You would have told him that in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have. We discussed similar things. A moment ago, in fact, I said what General Pasalic asked with respect to Makljen -- it's unrealistic to talk about Makljen. In the chain of command, I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, before we go for the break it seems that it's still unclear. In one zone of responsibility we have two, perhaps three, commanders and that is illogical. The military doesn't function this way; anybody -- everybody should know that. Perhaps we could ask a question to -- to the general: How is it they have three commanders in one zone of responsibility at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps we could deal with the problem as follows: Mr. Agic during the break could think things over and draw for us the hierarchy, the man from the 3rd Corps, the commander of the 317th Brigade, and the commander of the municipal defence staff; they all belong to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If he could list them in order of significance, of seniority, during the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need a break for that. I can tell you straight away. The commander of the 3rd Corps is General Enver Hadzihasanovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that. I'm talking about Cikotic, Selmo Cikotic. You and the commander of the 317th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Selmo Cikotic does not have command authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the municipality of Gornji Vakuf, show us the hierarchical chain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Heljic, Jusuf, was in command of the brigade. I was in command the municipal TO staff. On the 13th of January, the commander of the 3rd Corps, General Hadzihasanovic, appointed me as the senior officer in charge of the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Mr. Praljak, go ahead. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I can't understand why we're all trying to insist on the existence of a model that don't exist. Simply what exists in the French, English, or American army did not exist in Gornji Vakuf. It is true that Mr. Agic was in command of the town. It is true that Cikotic was his superior according to the hierarchy, but he couldn't give him commands but only Hadzihasanovic could. And again, you couldn't command to the brigade commander and so on. Isn't that so? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, General Praljak knows that the corps commander can compile a temporary set-up, and he may appoint a commander. In this particular case, he subordinated to me the 1st Battalion from the brigade, and I was in command of it because it was in town. Outside the town Colonel Heljic, Jusuf, commanded the units, and that is the truth. I think General Praljak is aware of the truth. And that is why I, as the most responsible person in town, was called to attend negotiations whenever there were problems within the area of the town. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] But on the other hand, this was a great problem for the HVO negotiators, who they would negotiate it with and whether an agreement would be implemented. I'm not talking about the psychology of Colonel Siljeg. I'm just saying that Colonel Andric and others found it very difficult sometimes to know exactly who is responsible for what, whom he has agreed with, and who he can criticise for not implementing a decision. Do you know that after the 14th or the 15th Colonel Andric never came to attend negotiations in UNPROFOR headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] We'll discuss that later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, can we make a provisional conclusion that you are in agreement with what has just been said by General Praljak with regard to the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said I stand by it. I was in command of forces in town and the chain of command was as I have described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, the last point that Mr. Praljak made was extremely critical, and I think we find this in Mr. Beese's account as well, where he says that the internationals constantly were trying to figure out who they had to deal with from the armija's side, who was in command, who was in charge; and I think this goes to the issues of negotiations. We need an answer from the gentleman on that aspect, that it would have been difficult from HVO to figure out who it is that is supposed to be negotiating, who has the ultimate authority, because this is the lack of confusion [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly. In your opinion, did the HVO have difficulty in knowing who was in fact in charge and in command on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, from the behaviour and statements of Colonel Siljeg, he knew very well who was in charge. It depended on his mood or the situation on the battlefront. He conducted the negotiations from the beginning to the end by Mr. Cikotic, and the agreement that was eventually signed by General Petkovic and General Arif Pasalic was prepared by Mr. Cikotic on behalf of the army. And all the documents then he signed could easily be implemented within the territory of Gornji Vakuf municipality there were no difficulties in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have a 20-minute break and we will resume then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Brigadier Agic, may we try and summarise what we discussed before the break, and it refers to the documents. You told me that the HVO documents that we discussed contain untruthful information, and that you told us that the documents of the BH army also contain erroneous information. Does that mean that all these documents of a military nature, regardless of the side they belong to, are not truthful?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I said that some of them were unrealistic and that they do not reflect the real state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: About unrealistic plans that are mentioned in Selmo Cikotic's report, the question was not whether they were realistic or unrealistic but whether they were plans or not. We need you to tell us that those plans existed.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not all plans.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So we don't need to make any kind of conclusion. Let us look at the documents which confirm what you have already told us and let us see that through the documents that attempts were made by peaceful means to deal with the conflict and that orders were issued to cease fire. Would you please look at my set of documents, P 01211. It is a Prosecution document. It is an order by Mate Boban. In my set of documents, Brigadier Agic. In --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know who Mr. Mate Boban was?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Mate Boban was president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did he have a position in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. He was the Supreme Commander of the HVO. So Mr. Mate Boban, dated the 19th of January, 1993. "With a view to stopping conflicts between the Croatian and Muslim peoples I hereby issue an order prohibiting offensive operations." Tell me, please, were you aware of the fact that the Supreme Commander of the HVO had issued such an order?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to look at document D01238 -- P, sorry P 01238. I hope you will be familiar with this document. You mentioned it. It is an order, which on the 20th of January, 1993, was signed by Milivoj Petkovic and Arif Pasalic, ordering a cease-fire establishing contacts for a peaceful solution of the conflict and so on. Were you aware of this order?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I should now like to draw your attention to document 4D 00048. It is an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I wish to go back to the previous order, the order signed by the 20th of January -- on the 20th of January by General Petkovic. In point 1 it says that combat operations between the HVO and the BH army must simultaneously and unconditionally be ended in the entire territory of Gornji Vakuf. I see after that there's an order to stop the artillery. Does this document show that the HVO had artillery at its disposal, which is described in the same line in English, field gun, MB mortar, and tanks. The artillery described by General Petkovic, does it correspond with the an artillery the HVO had on the ground?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the rest. Only the multiple rocket-launchers are missing. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I make an additional remark. This order is not simply signed. There are two signatories on this order. In the paragraph you are quoting, it doesn't say who the equipment belonged to, and no mention is made who they belonged to, nor their numbers or quantities; therefore, it is not my order. It is an order by Arif Pasalic on behalf of the Supreme Command Staff. So he signed this command, together with me, on behalf of Sefer Halilovic. So I just wish to add that these are -- this is not my order or my equipment. That is the equipment of the HVO. This applies to the equipment on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think there is any dispute over the co-signatories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. General Petkovic has clarified a point. He tells us that the materiel and the artillery belong to both parties. Did the BH in Gornji Vakuf have a tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not only in Gornji Vakuf, but in the territory of the whole municipality there wasn't a single tank. The army did not have a tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I asked you to look at document 4D 00048. If you can't find it --

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a report?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's a short order dated the 24th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D 00048. You have it now in electronic form. You can look at it. It is an order by Milivoj Petkovic. On the 24th of January he was in Geneva attending negotiations, and it has -- on the future structure of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And he issued an order of the following contents: "HVO units in Gornji Vakuf shall stop offensive activities against units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina immediately." And under 2: "The order issued by the president of the HZ HB, Mate Boban, issued on the 19th of January, 1993, shall be fully obeyed, as well as my order of the 20th of January, 1993." Tell me, did you know that on the 24th the military leadership of the HVO issued such an order from Geneva on the cessation of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A cease-fire agreement was signed after this, that is on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Will you please look in -- at a document in my set, P 01329. It is a joint statement by Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban in Geneva. So: "The supreme commanders have agreed on the cessation of the conflict between the BH army and the HVO. The commanders of the Main Staff of the army and of the HVO are called upon to determine the responsibility for the outbreak of the fighting at all levels and form a Joint Command without delay." Tell me, were you aware of this joint statement in Vakuf? Were you informed about it?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A similar order was issued after the order issued by General Petkovic and Arif Pasalic, a similar order was issued by the 3rd Corps on an unconditional cessation of hostilities and there was a truce signed on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have a look at 4D 00358. This is an order issued by Milivoj Petkovic, as the chief of the HVO Main Staff, and with regard to this joint statement from Mr. Boban and Mr. Izetbegovic and HVO units forbidden to launch attacks of any kind and they asked to negotiate. You mentioned a similar order issued by the ABiH corps. Were the contents of the order similar?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Bench now allow my client, Mr. Milivoj Petkovic, to put a few questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Agic. Cross-examination by the Accused Petkovic:

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Agic, I've few questions. Let's back to the year 1992. The neighbouring municipality of Gornji Vakuf is Kupres?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Through Radusa and Dolac?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the Serbs and the JNA attacked Kupres?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I know the time-period. It was the first day of Bajram; it was in March.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can I correct you?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It wasn't in March. Let's agree that it was in the first half of April.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought it was at the end of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you send your forces in to confront the JNA forces and the Serbian aggressor?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You didn't. Where is Kupres located, in Croatia or Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kupres is in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So the JNA launched an attack, expelled the Croats and the Muslims from Kupres. About a hundred Croats were captured, about 50 were killed, and you were sitting in your municipality calmly?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't take any decisions at our level as to whether we would go to Kupres or not; that was an issue for someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. After Kupres had been taken, tell me whether Bugojno and Gornji Vakuf and Prozor were a threat, and I won't even mention Livno and Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that it would be realistic to say that Bugojno was under threat; Vakuf, to a lesser extent; and that's also the case with Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's what you claim. Now, tell me, after the fall of Kupres, did you take over the lines towards the Army of Republika Srpska, let's say in the direction of Radusa?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what happened around the 20th of June when there was a clash or an incident between the HVO and the TO?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me be specific. Did you withdraw your forces from Radusa to go into a conflict with the HVO on the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you receive an order to return your forces to Radusa?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the juncture with HVO, because the armija or the Territorial Defence had withdrawn to the right, so Voljica was empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at 4D 00378.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D 00378. I think it will appear on the screen. Are you familiar with this document? It's the president of the Municipal Assembly of Gornji Vakuf, and it says: "We hereby order the TO command in Gornji Vakuf to return its armed forces to the area of Radusa. The commander of the TO in Gornji Vakuf is responsible for carrying out the order." Is that what it says: Is it a correct document?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that this document is in order. I must admit that I haven't seen this document before. The then-commander of the TO must have received it, but I can claim that some of the positions to the right of Radusa, the Dragus -- Raduski Kamen up to Oglavak had been abandoned. That's a fairly wide area that was taken back later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was after the decision for you to return. Do you know that a day prior to the conflict in Prozor from the Idovac position the ABiH in fact abandoned that position and reported to the troops in Vakuf, and Mr. Grujic commanded those forces?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that. He reported to Voljica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. You told us that at the time of the conflict in Prozor you visited that area, the area of Mejnik, Crni Vrh, Makljen, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a witness who has appeared here said that the HVO, or rather, the ABiH in Prozor didn't killed the HVO soldier, and that was apparently the reason for the conflict. He said that it was troops from Gornji Vakuf. I don't know if they were under your command at the time.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if that had been -- and that was the reason for the conflict in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It provoked the conflict.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the commander of the staff was in Gornji Vakuf earlier on, Muharem Saric, and there were no signs that there would be a conflict in Prozor. I know that you had joint people from Radusa to Zvindeca [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did Sabic come to see you to implement the so-called plan B?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim with full responsibility, General, that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We have evidence here and we have other documents, according to which your forces from Gornji Vakuf were bearing down on Prozor from Crni Vrh, Mejnik, and Vakuf. We'll prove that.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps you didn't participate in it. Do you know that up to the 21st when the military police and the forces led by Prkacin -- well, who issued an order according to which they shouldn't be allowed to pass through Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 21st of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of October, I issued an order and this had been issued by the commander of the 3rd Corps, because a conflict in Novi Travnik had started.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You say it was no Novi Travnik, but we are saying that Ante Prkacin on the police were sent September to Jajce, but you say you stopped them?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we stopped them because they were ordered to be stopped

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down for the interpreters, please. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's good to know that; that's a historical truth. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Agic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions on behalf of General Petkovic. I'll now give the floor to the other Defence teams. We have another 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Praljak will be conducting this cross-examination. We believe that it would be more appropriate for a soldier to cross-examine a soldier. We think it will be more useful for the Chamber. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you Your Honours. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I hope we'll both be able to move along quickly and that we'll be able to clarify certain contentious issues. Given time restriction, I'd be grateful if you could provided brief answers; and if we require explanations, I'll ask you for such explanations. Do you know that immediately after the conflict in Prozor I went to that territory?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that after that event I stayed until the 24th of December, 1992, in the area of Rama and Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, Novi Travnik, and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because on the 4th of December you were at a meeting in Gornji Vakuf at Bozo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- I believe that you don't, but I'll ask you this question after all. Do you know that I was in that territory at the time, as agreed with Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mr. Franjo Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that I tried to calm down that situation that was simmering all the time; we'll see what way in the documents. Do you know that I asked for Mr. Andric, who was from Bijelo Polje near Mostar and who did excellent work in Bijelo Polje, do you know that I transferred him to Bugojno in order for him to calm the situation down and try to establish a Joint Command? Were you familiar with these attempts?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Andric, and I do believe that he was in favour of such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know at the time I insisted on the establishment of a Joint Command? Do you know that we had a joint stamp, a stamp that we used in common, and I asked for Sefer Halilovic to come, and we were aware of the fact that if two armies didn't join up a conflict would break out between them because of various individuals, et cetera? Were you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With some of it, yes, but not all of it. But I know that attempts were made; whether these attempts were in good faith. Whether the attempts to establish a Joint Command were done in good faith I don't know, but I know that attempts had been made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will refer to the map that I've drawn also later on, but for the moment I'd like to clarify some other issues. You know that an aggression was launched by the JNA and the Serbs in 1991. This also included paramilitary formation and it was directed against Croatia?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And you know that from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, or rather, the territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time was used to launch attacks against Croatia from that territory?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also know that at that time Croatia was burning, it had lost about a third of its territory, and there were many Muslim Bosniak refugees at the time who had been expelled from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and they had found refuge in Croatia, that included the sick, women and children, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the time throughout the year 1991 in Bosnia and Herzegovina, for reasons that we can understand, for reasons that Mr. Izetbegovic had, well, Bosnia and Herzegovina remained passive. It didn't join in the war. It didn't issue mobilisation orders. It didn't ask for its citizens to remain in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to remain in a state of readiness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know that the collective head of state in Bosnia-Herzegovina found it difficult to take such decisions. I know that many citizens did take in Croatian citizens, provided them with accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I know about all of that. Let's have 3D 00539 on the ELMO or on the screen.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I can't see that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It will appear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 3D 00539. That's my document. At the request of my Defence - and this was also my desire - I obtained the following information. I'd like to clarify an important problem that has appeared before the Court. It concerns the Croatian army in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is a recurrent issue. Sir, I'd like to demonstrate how many citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina participated in the defence of Croatia when the attack was launched in 1991 and 1992, up until the time that war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, although this had already started in Unista, et cetera. Here it says: "Out of 490.000 who were Croatian defenders, 58.065 were born outside of the Republic of Croatia, out of which 41.097 were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina." As for 8.929 individuals there is no information you can see that here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Out of a total of 163.954 volunteers - we're talking about volunteers, people not mobilised by the state because the state of Croatia department exist in legal terms at the time - out of that number 16.802 were born outside of Croatia, of which 12.436 were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's what it says here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And could we have a look at the following document, please 3D 00540. And similarly, we have this document here in the MUP of the Republic of Croatia. There were 2.246 members born in Bosnia-Herzegovina; that's what it says here. In the defence of Dubrovnik, 320 members of the MUP were participants and they were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Nine out of this total number were killed. So was Zrinko Zuljevic Klica one of such men who went to Croatia and then returned?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: He said something about you -- or he told you initially that he had come to defend Kupres in fact. That's what he said?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1994 he lost his leg at Kupres?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Praljak, a minor question. I was looking at this document with interest, the document addressed to your lawyer by the Republic of Croatia, and I noticed that the document 540 mentions highly confidential, or rather, secret, very secret. The Government of Republic of Croatia has authorised you to make this document public? Because we are in open session the document is on the screen. Mr. Kovacic, as far as the question of secrecy is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Ministry of Justice and the Republic of Croatia has established a rule, according to which these documents are secret until they are disclosed to the Defence that has the right to use them in court. They're not asking for these documents to remain secret. This information is no longer classified; it should be treated as confidential, but that is not the case when these documents are being used at court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, but the fact that certain documents are secret will be very detrimental to our case. Could we see the following documents: 3D 00438 -- 483, 3D 00483. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document you will see that there is a battalion, Bruno Busic, that has the name of Ahmet Memisevic, a Muslim, a Bosniak. Could we see that on the screen, and the date is the 20th of June, 1992. And that it says: "Today in the territory of Gornji Vakuf" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the registrar tells me that this document has not been registered in e-court, so if you wish to show the document under the ELMO, it should be placed under the ELMO. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes, please. Could I ask the usher for his assistance. Your Honours, do you have the English translation of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's not in the binder of documents. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]. Can we see the document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: "In a four-hour-long struggle, two members of the HVO were killed and several wounded." So there was a conflict with two men dead and a member of the unit was also killed. Does it say that here?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So there was a conflict. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next document, please, 3D 00490, 3D 00490.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it a report? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, a report on the events in the territory of our municipality from the 20th to the 21st of June, 1992. And it says the following -- I will ask you whether it is correct. "We didn't have any particular plan of armed conflict claims the HVO. Immediately before the attacks by the so-called Green Berets between 02 and 04, a major incident occurred when they broke into apartments searching and mistreating the inhabitants. They captured a civilian -- civilians of Croat ethnicity, used them as a human shield. They did this to travellers going to Austria, taking them off buses. All this was done by the Green Berets. The behaviour towards the inhabitants has certain elements of Chetnik policies. Before the attack, the TO pulled out all the manpower with its weapons from the sector of Radusa, where they were securing the lines against Chetnik attacks." That is what it stated in this report. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the day, and I can claim, at least for our side, the TO, that we didn't have any concrete plan and I believe that the HVO didn't either. But I cannot agree that they behaved in this way and that they broke into houses; I claim with responsibility that they didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Brigadier, I have no doubt -- reason to doubt what you're saying, I'm just reading this report. Now, this brings us to something that we need to clear up. In answer to a question from Judge Antonetti as to who first started shooting in town, your answer was the HVO.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this date it was the HVO who started shooting first.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But not on this day, in January in town?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting in June in town, in October, in November, but on the 12th or 11th of January occurred. And this was confirmed on the 12th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My question is: Were you on the spot when the shooting started? Were you personally on the spot when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Any one.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of January, I was in the street close to the shells that fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about shells; I'm talking infantry fire.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shooting in the centre of town came later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So when your lower-level commanders and fighters said without any doubt when asked who started first that it was the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as yours told you that it was the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When Tokic or someone else asked: For heaven's sake, who started shooting? They say the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina attacked us. Is that right? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And you yourself said here to calm down those conflicts the commanders invested a great deal of energy. When they calmed one set, a new fire would break out in Novi Travnik; then it went to Gornji Vakuf, from Gornji Vakuf to Prozor, and so on. Was it like that?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Not only was -- did the conflict spread. And another matter that we know happened, a third of the army was on the lines, a third was on leave, and a third was on the alert, and many of them sat around in bars waiting around. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And they talked. And as an incident occurred, the stories became worse and worse and more damaging for the opposite side. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Things were exaggerated, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And then you would hear sentences such as these, because the Judges need to hear them. They would read something like this -- I wrote them down so I can read them for you. The Croats would say something like this: Fuck their balija mothers. Look what they're doing to us. They don't stick to their word. They will trick us. Is this what the Croats would say frequently? Yes, Mr. Agic. We're entitled to say these things.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people I worked with never said such things. I didn't go to bars, but I assume that was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Agic, believe me, you should have been in bars.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain why I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that on another occasion. On your side they would say: Fuck their Ustasha mothers. Look what they're going to do to us. They're going to expel us. They're going to kill us.

utterances.speaker: FAHRUDIN AGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that because I heard statements of that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And every time there was more -- a greater and greater lack of confidence.
